reasoning: While the fidelity scores are high (0.9781), the identified concern regarding full-page content duplication is a significant structural defect. The report indicates the entire poster sequence appears twice with an extra text block in between, which creates a poor user experience and potential confusion for assistive technology. Human review is required to resolve this duplication before publication.

concerns.analysis: The entire content of the poster is duplicated on the page. The sequence of elements (Heading, mask graphic, body text, blue call-to-action box, and department logo) appears twice. There is also a small block of plain text between the two repetitions that reproduces the body text for a third time.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: The source document consists of a single set of informational elements: 'Wear a Mask' heading, mask graphic, 'We appreciate your cooperation' text, blue vaccine CTA box, and the NC DHHS logo.
concerns.output_quote: The HTML screenshot shows the complete set of poster elements (Wear a Mask, mask graphic, text, blue box, logo) appearing at the top, followed by a text block, and then the entire set of elements is repeated in full again further down the page.
concerns.location: Main content area, repeated twice sequentially.

action_items: Determine why the content was duplicated during conversion.
Remove redundant content blocks so the HTML reflects a single-page poster as intended.
Verify that the final structure is logical for screen reader users.
quality_score_note: Blended 0-100 score combining fidelity evaluation (40%), text matching (20%), content completeness (15%), accessibility compliance (10%), and decision confidence (15%). Routing decisions are based on fidelity scores above, not this score.
